title: Division as a missing multiplication
objectives: Divide by asking which number multiplies up to the target.
Divide past the table by splitting, halving, or doubling then dividing by 10

screens.title: Division as a missing multiplication
screens.prose: Every division hides a multiplication you already know. We will find it, and when the numbers get too big, break them into pieces you can handle.
This is the times table up to $12 \times 12$. Column 7 holds the 7 times table. The question is $84 \div 7$: how many 7s make 84?
screens.question: Tap the cell in column 7 that holds 84.

hints.text: Count down column 7 in steps of 7: 7, 14, 21, and so on.
84 sits near the bottom of the column.
$7 \times 10 = 70$ and $7 \times 2 = 14$, so $7 \times 12 = 84$. Look in row 12.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find 84 in column 7, then read the number at the start of its row.

byKey.r11c7: That cell holds 77, which is $7 \times 11$. You need one more 7.
byKey.r10c7: That cell holds 70, which is $7 \times 10$. You need two more 7s.
byKey.r7c7: That cell holds 49, which is $7 \times 7$. Keep going down the column.

explain.text: You found 84 in column 7, in row 12, because $7 \times 12 = 84$. So $84 \div 7 = 12$: the row number is the answer. The division was a multiplication with one number missing.

screens.prose: The same number can sit in several places in the table. Each place gives its own division facts. Tap a cell to mark it, and tap again to clear it.
screens.question: Tap every cell that holds 72.

hints.text: Which pairs of numbers up to 12 multiply to 72?
Try the 8 times table first.
$72 = 8 \times 9 = 6 \times 12$. Each pair appears twice, once each way round.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Look for 72 in every column, not just one.

byKey.one-way-a: You found each pair one way round. $9 \times 8$ and $12 \times 6$ are separate cells.
byKey.one-way-b: You found each pair one way round. $8 \times 9$ and $6 \times 12$ are separate cells.
byKey.pair-only: You found $8 \times 9$ both ways. $6 \times 12$ also makes 72.

explain.text: You found 72 four times. The cell in row 8, column 9 gives $72 \div 8 = 9$ and $72 \div 9 = 8$. The cells in rows 6 and 12 give $72 \div 6 = 12$ and $72 \div 12 = 6$.

screens.prose: Both times you turned a division round: $84 \div 7$ became $7 \times ? = 84$. We call the hidden number the **missing factor**. It is the answer to the division.
screens.question: What is $108 \div 9$?

hints.text: What times 9 makes 108?
Look near the bottom of column 9.
$9 \times 10 = 90$ and $9 \times 2 = 18$. Together that is $9 \times 12 = 108$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Ask which number times 9 makes 108.

explain.text: You asked $9 \times ? = 108$. Since $9 \times 12 = 108$, the missing factor is 12. So $108 \div 9 = 12$.

screens.prose: Now $96 \div 4$. The 4 times table stops at 48, so 96 is off the table. Picture a rectangle 4 tall with area 96, cut into $80 + 16$.
screens.question: How wide is each piece? Then give the whole width.

hints.text: Each piece is 4 tall. What width gives an area of 80?
$4 \times 20 = 80$ and $4 \times 4 = 16$.
The widths are 20 and 4. The whole rectangle is $20 + 4 = 24$ wide.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Divide each piece by the height 4, then add the widths.

byKey.r2c1: The pieces sit side by side, so the whole width is the two widths added.

explain.text: You divided each piece by 4: $80 \div 4 = 20$ and $16 \div 4 = 4$. The pieces sit side by side, so the whole width is $20 + 4 = 24$. Splitting works because both pieces share the height 4.

canvas.caption: Widths 20 and 4: the whole width is 24

screens.prose: Another route for $\div 4$. Since $4 = 2 \times 2$, dividing by 4 is halving, then halving again. Here is $136 \div 4$, with the first halving drawn.
screens.question: Drag the blue point to $136 \div 4$.

hints.text: Half of 136 is 68. What is half of 68?
Half of 60 is 30, and half of 8 is 4.
Half of 68 is 34. Drag the point to 34.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Halve 68 once more and drag the point there.

byKey.once: That is 68, one halving. Dividing by 4 needs a second halving.
byKey.thrice: That is 17, three halvings, which divides by 8. Stop after two.
byKey.q: Halve 68: half of 60 is 30 and half of 8 is 4.

explain.text: You halved 136 to 68, then 68 to 34. Two halvings divide by $2 \times 2 = 4$, so $136 \div 4 = 34$. Check: $34 \times 4 = 136$.

screens.prose: Now divide by 5. A 5 is half a 10, so any number holds twice as many 5s as 10s. The line doubles 115 to 230.
screens.question: What is $115 \div 5$?

hints.text: How many 10s are there in 230?
Doubling gives 230, and $230 \div 10 = 23$. Check: $23 \times 5 = 115$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Double 115, then divide by 10.

byKey.doubled-only: 230 is the doubled number. Divide it by 10 to finish.
byKey.tenth-only: 11.5 is $115 \div 10$. There are twice as many 5s as 10s, so double it.
byKey.halved: 57.5 is half of 115, which is $115 \div 2$. Divide by 5, not by 2.

explain.text: Doubling 115 gave 230, and 230 holds 23 tens. A 5 is half a 10, so 115 holds 23 fives as well. Check: $23 \times 5 = 115$.

screens.prose: A friend works out $84 \div 12$ like this: $84 \div 10 = 8.4$ and $84 \div 2 = 42$, so the answer is $8.4 + 42 = 50.4$. The rectangle has area 84 and height $12 = 10 + 2$.
screens.question: What is $84 \div 12$?

options.why: You split the 12 into $10 + 2$ and added both answers. The 10 strip and the 2 strip share one width, so their answers do not add.
You recalled $84 \div 7 = 12$. Here 12 is the divisor, so the answer is the other factor.
You divided by 10 only. The height is 12, so the width is less than 8.4.

hints.text: What times 12 makes 84?
The two strips are 10 tall and 2 tall, and they share one width.
$12 \times 7 = 84$. The strips hold $10 \times 7 = 70$ and $2 \times 7 = 14$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Ask which number times 12 makes 84.

byKey.split-divisor: You split the 12 into $10 + 2$ and added. The two strips share one width, so their answers do not add.

explain.text: Cutting the height 12 into 10 and 2 makes two strips with the same width, 7. Your friend's sum adds two widths that are really one. Split the number being divided, never the divisor.

screens.prose: Here is what you did. A division asks for a missing factor: $$a \div b = c \quad \text{means} \quad b \times c = a$$ Off the table, split $a$ into multiples of $b$: $$(x + y) \div b = x \div b + y \div b$$ Halving twice divides by 4. Doubling, then dividing by 10, divides by 5.
screens.question: Which split of $156 \div 12$ is safe?

options.why: That splits the divisor 12. Only the number being divided can be split.
You divided the first piece and forgot the second. Both pieces must be divided by 12.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Split the 156, and divide every piece by 12.

explain.text: 120 and 36 are both multiples of 12, so each piece divides cleanly, giving 10 and 3. Adding gives 13. Check: $12 \times 13 = 156$.

screens.prose: Dividing by 8 is three halvings, because $8 = 2 \times 2 \times 2$. Put the working for $184 \div 8$ in order.
screens.question: Put the lines in order.

hints.text: Which line rewrites the 8 before any halving?
Each halving uses up one 2 from the bracket.
Start with 8 as $2 \times 2 \times 2$. Then halve: 184, 92, 46, 23.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Rewrite the 8 first, then halve once per line.

explain.text: Each halving removes one 2 from the 8, so the bracket shrinks by one factor per line. After three halvings nothing is left to divide by. Check: $23 \times 8 = 184$.

screens.prose: You bought 8 shares of one stock. The contract note shows the total cost before fees.
screens.question: What did each share cost?

hints.text: Dividing by 8 is three halvings.
764 halves to 382, then to 191.
Half of 191 is 95.5. Each share cost £95.50.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Halve £764.00 three times.

byKey.two-halvings: 191 is two halvings, which divides by 4. Dividing by 8 needs a third.
byKey.remainder-digit: Half of 191 is 95 remainder 1, and that 1 is £1 shared by 2. So the price is £95.50, not £95.10.
byKey.one-halving: 382 is one halving, which divides by 2. Halve twice more.

explain.text: You halved three times: 764, 382, 191, then 95.50. The last halving splits the odd £1 into two 50p halves. Check: $8 \times 95.50 = 764$.

ideas: A division asks for a missing factor: $84 \div 7$ asks $7 \times ? = 84$.
Off the table, split the number being divided into multiples of the divisor: $96 = 80 + 16$, so $96 \div 4 = 20 + 4$.
Halve twice to divide by 4 and three times to divide by 8. For 5, double, then divide by 10.

formula.name: Splitting a division
formula.tex: (x + y) \div b = x \div b + y \div b
formula.note: Split the number you divide, never the divisor.

summary.trap: $84 \div 12$ is not $84 \div 10 + 84 \div 2$. Splitting the divisor adds two widths that are really one.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Ask which number times 6 makes 72.

explain.text: The missing factor in $6 \times ? = 72$ is 12. So $72 \div 6 = 12$.

quiz.prose: In a default Zetamac round, division answers go up to 100.
quiz.question: What is $700 \div 7$?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Ask which number times 7 makes 700.

explain.text: $7 \times 100 = 700$, so the missing factor is 100. The zeros carry straight across: $7 \div 7 = 1$, then two zeros.

quiz.prose: Use the shortcut for dividing by 5.
quiz.question: What is $135 \div 5$?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Double 135, then divide by 10.

byKey.doubled-only: 270 is the doubled number. Divide by 10 to finish.
byKey.tenth-only: 13.5 is $135 \div 10$. There are twice as many 5s as 10s, so double it.

explain.text: Doubling gives 270, which holds 27 tens. A 5 is half a 10, so 135 holds 27 fives. Check: $27 \times 5 = 135$.

quiz.prose: Four people try $192 \div 8$ in their heads.
quiz.question: Whose working is right?

options.why: Two halvings divide by 4, not 8. A third halving is needed.
That splits the divisor 8 into $4 + 4$. Only the number being divided can be split.
The 32 was never divided by 8. Both pieces need dividing.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count how many halvings dividing by 8 needs.

explain.text: Since $8 = 2 \times 2 \times 2$, dividing by 8 is three halvings: 96, 48, 24. Check: $24 \times 8 = 192$.
